summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, prior stents, diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for shortness of breath, fatigue, and pleuritic chest pain. Initial evaluation revealed an elevated D-dimer, and a CT pulmonary angiogram confirmed bilateral pulmonary emboli. A lower extremity ultrasound showed an acute deep vein thrombosis in the left common femoral vein. Troponins and BNP were normal, and EKG showed no acute changes. He was started on heparin and transitioned to warfarin with Lovenox bridging. The patient remained stable on room air, with persistent mild dyspnea on exertion leading to a two-night stay. He was discharged home on anticoagulation with instructions for INR monitoring and further evaluation for an unprovoked thrombotic event.
